feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform leadership, with clear domain focus and solid evidence of progression and scope. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive, and could sharpen impact by prioritizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience align well around digital platform modernization, governance, analytics, and communications leadership.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure at NACo with visible progression, relevant tools, and concrete scale indicators like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and “50+ internal publishers.”  
- Broad yet coherent skill set: combines strategy, technical execution, analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia in a way that fits senior public-sector digital roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition: “digital strategy,” “workflows,” “governance,” and “content operations” recur across sections; consolidate Core Competencies, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT to avoid overlap.  
- Increase impact language: several bullets describe duties rather than results; add more measurable outcomes such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; punctuation style varies across bullets/sections; “French (A2/Learning)” is slightly awkward—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings or grammar errors found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. Tightening the language and foregrounding the most distinctive strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for high-volume, mission-driven public-sector organizations. Expertise spans digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with “modernizing enterprise web ecosystems” for sharper, more senior phrasing.
- Change “Leads” to “Expertise spans” or “Specializes in” to avoid sentence-fragment feel and improve flow.
- Keep the intro focused on strategic scope; let work experience carry specifics like Drupal, page volume, and audience scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Senior digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- “Governance models,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” repeat core competencies almost verbatim.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas with more parallel phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, category-style phrases and keep structure parallel; e.g.: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization • Multi-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” or “user experience” for clearer meaning.
- Consider “communications leadership” instead of “communications operations” to better reflect seniority.
- Standardize style: either use “and” throughout or “&” throughout; “and” reads more polished.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific or project-specific wording.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” is close to language already used in the header and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshots, but the footer repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing distinct outcomes or formats will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed [project] to [purpose/outcome].”
- Tighten wording: change “Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining…” to “Built an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content, and bill-level chat.”
- Standardize style and punctuation: use “10 x 20-foot” (not “10×20-foot”) and consider “multi-part”/“bill-level” consistently.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current and NACo roles; keep only if framed as selected examples, not repeated duties.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider leading with it to reduce repetition.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and project footer. Tighten it around 4–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or scope wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading web modernization, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, standardized, optimized.
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences, including modular microsites and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved enterprise web operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and publishing systems for coordinated cross-team communications.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content models, and user discovery experience.
- Provided front-end/CMS implementation and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/users, publishing teams supported, reduction in turnaround time, engagement lift, search success improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let projects hold the detail.
- Governance/analytics/workflows also echo prior NACo roles, so emphasize what is new in this current engagement.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to foreground enterprise outcomes and distinguish this director-level role from the earlier NACo positions. Emphasize transformation, team/operating leadership, and measurable business impact over channel lists.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, budget, and multi-channel communications across web, email, social, and video.”
- Rewrite bullets to stress outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable impact where possible for email/social/video/analytics: subscriber growth, engagement lift, reporting speed, production cost savings, or reduced reliance on vendors after launching the in-house studio.
- Combine softer bullets for concision: merge governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning into one operational-improvement bullet.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; keep this one at strategic/organizational level, not day-to-day execution.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; keep the CV item focused on leadership and capacity created.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to operational ownership, editorial systems, and channel growth during this period.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Clarify the video contribution with impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper systems bullet: “Improved editorial planning, cross-team coordination and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations…” is very close to the Director role’s opening; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/formalizing the series.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should sharpen the leadership/value angle and use tighter phrasing that reflects recent enterprise-scale work.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, outcome-oriented wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector platforms
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging for mission-driven organizations
- Audience-centered content planning and campaign storytelling
- Consider dropping “leadership” from the heading or shortening to “Digital Strategy & Content Operations” for concision.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing broad concepts with soft descriptors like “audience-focused.”
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale already proven in experience (10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Core Competencies (“Digital governance & editorial systems,” “Multi-channel communications operations,” “Advocacy and public-sector communications”).
- “Enterprise digital strategy” is already implied in the header summary.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill mix, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes rather than repeat a software inventory.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery experiences”
- Remove lower-signal or dated items here, especially “jQuery,” unless it is essential for target roles.
- Put the strongest, most recent differentiators first: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, workflow automation.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization and migration” instead of just “CMS modernization.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT”; avoid listing the same platforms verbatim in both places.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” already appears in Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct or shorten here.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a senior-level capability statement. It should emphasize decision support and optimization outcomes, especially since recent experience already proves hands-on platform depth.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to leadership-level capability: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio and Microsoft Clarity for analytics infrastructure, KPI frameworks and executive reporting.”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “executive dashboards and decision-support reporting.”
- Tighten “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and content performance optimization” if accurate.
- Consider revised version: “Analytics infrastructure (GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity) • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and reporting • SEO, UX and content performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and less tool-dense.
- “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating that exact phrasing.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize delivery capability and recent leadership-level multimedia work rather than listing basic production tasks.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Multimedia Production, Studio & Event Delivery**
- Replace with tighter, higher-value phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations  
- Virtual event delivery and technical run-of-show support
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: **Built and operated an in-house broadcast-quality studio supporting advocacy programming and event coverage**
- Keep terms consistent with recent roles: use “hybrid event production” and “studio operations” to align with NACo/consulting experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing.
- Tool-specific detail is better left to “Multimedia & Creative Tools,” so don’t over-expand software/hardware here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either sharpen platform depth or be condensed to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize strongest/recent platforms first: “Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- If space allows, add level/context instead of just names: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a notable project; it feels lighter than the rest and may dilute seniority.
- Keep naming consistent with the CV’s impact language; “enterprise Drupal” or “Drupal 10” would better align with recent experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2], which already lists the same platforms plus broader technical capabilities.
- If both sections stay, use Topline Skills for strategic breadth and this item only for platform names with proficiency/context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; they add little value for a senior candidate.
- Consider renaming the heading to “Front-End & Implementation Tools” to better match the content and sound less junior.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one brief proof point tied to recent work, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, workflow automation, and lightweight serverless functions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the exact phrasing in both places.
- GitHub Actions may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” if you want this section purely implementation-focused.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow design leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more systems-oriented.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strongest/relevant tools first: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If space allows, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If you have proof points elsewhere, consider replacing one lower-value tool with a capability phrase: **Airtable systems • workflow automation • cross-team planning tools**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating those exact phrases too often.
- Slack/Teams are common workplace tools; keep them only if collaboration platforms are important to the target role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this line should stay tool-focused and, if possible, signal enterprise-level use rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform naming for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope/level to make it stronger without becoming a work-history bullet: **Enterprise email campaign delivery, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first to reflect recency/relevance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding phrases like “managed newsletters” or “led email strategy”; those are already covered in Work Experience.
- Be careful with “engagement” wording if you can’t support CRM/community outcomes elsewhere on the CV.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a generic list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In the Technical + IT section, it should read as a concise tools/category line rather than repeat broader competency language.

Suggested edit:
- Tighten to platform/tool names plus one or two technical methods: “GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing”
- Replace vague “Dashboarding” with the actual tools already listed, or “KPI reporting” if you want a capability term.
- Consider swapping “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “technical SEO” to make it more concrete and tool-oriented.
- If space allows, order by strongest/recently used tools first: “GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is nearly identical to “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; differentiate this section as tools-only.
- “Dashboarding” duplicates Looker Studio/Power BI, so it adds little value.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early digital operations, and concrete outputs rather than repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 concrete outputs or scale markers if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or frequency.
- Tighten the close to show people/process impact: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates while providing day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Consider a sharper version: “Promoted across two roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, support a major website refresh, and establish repeatable production workflows across web, email, social, and video.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; differentiate this as the launch/build phase.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already covered more strongly in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project coordination, and trim broad phrases like “supporting organizational programs and policy work.”

Suggested edit:
- Reframe around distinct contributions: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives for county-focused programs and policy teams…”
- Make the podcast the lead accomplishment: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- Tighten multimedia language: replace “Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with “Produced digital and multimedia content supporting program and policy communications.”
- Add scope or outcomes if available: number of episodes, audiences served, teams supported, or research/project outputs delivered.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad digital/media responsibilities already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- “Multimedia production” and “digital content” are recurring themes elsewhere; keep this entry focused on innovation/research coordination + first podcast launch.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so it should be tightened to emphasize tools only or clearly separate tools from production specialties.

Suggested edit:
- Split software from production capabilities for cleaner scanning.
